questions.question: How do flowering plants reproduce?
options: Asexually only, by forming spores
Sexually, involving male and female gametes
Only through vegetative propagation of roots
By budding off new independent structures

questions.question: Why is plant reproduction vital for life on Earth?
options: Plants are producers that provide the primary food source for all animals.
It keeps the soil temperature stable across different climates.
It is the only way that carbon dioxide is released into the atmosphere.
Plants require animals to reproduce in order to clean the water supply.

questions.question: What name is given to the female gametes in plants?
options: Pollen grains
Anthers
Egg cells (ova)
Ovary walls

questions.question: Which plant structures carry the male gametes?
options: Egg cells
Pollen grains
Stigmas
Petals

questions.question: What are the three main components of a seed, and where are seeds formed?
options: Embryo, food store, and tough outer coat; formed in the ovary
Pollen, nectar, and petals; formed in the anther
Root, stem, and leaf; formed in the pollen tube
Spores, chlorophyll, and cell wall; formed in the stigma

questions.question: Which of the following best describes what a fruit is?
options: The dried up petals of a pollinated flower
The mature and ripened ovary of a seed-producing plant
The swollen root system of a flowering plant
A collection of pollen grains bonded together by nectar

questions.question: What is the primary role of a pollinator in plant reproduction?
options: To disperse mature seeds away from the parent plant
To transfer pollen from one flower to another to enable sexual reproduction
To digest nectar and convert it into plant hormones
To provide warmth to the soil surrounding the plant roots

questions.question: Which group of animals constitutes the majority of pollinators, and which specific group within them is the largest?
options: Birds, with hummingbirds being the largest group
Insects, with bees being the largest group
Mammals, with bats being the largest group
Reptiles, with lizards being the largest group

questions.question: What is meant by the term 'food security'?
options: Having enough affordable and nutritious food in an area or country
The lockable storage of food supplies to prevent theft
The chemical preservation of food to increase its shelf life
Restricting food consumption to only locally grown crops

questions.question: Why must pollinating insects be protected from pesticides, climate change, and habitat loss?
options: To prevent them from mutating into new species
To ensure global food security by maintaining crop pollination
To stop them from eating too many agricultural crops
To allow them to produce more honey for international trade

questions.question: What is pollination?
options: The release of seeds from the mature fruit into the wind
The fusion of the nuclei of the male and female gametes
The transfer of pollen from the male anther to the female stigma
The growth of a pollen tube down through the style

questions.question: What are the two types of pollination, and which type increases variation in a species?
options: Wind pollination and animal pollination; wind pollination increases variation
Self-pollination and cross-pollination; cross-pollination increases variation
Internal pollination and external pollination; internal pollination increases variation
Direct pollination and indirect pollination; direct pollination increases variation

questions.question: What occurs during plant fertilisation?
options: Pollen is transferred from the anther to the stigma of the flower.
The seed coat hardens to protect the embryo inside.
The nuclei of the male and female gametes fuse together.
The flower petals drop off to allow the fruit to ripen.

questions.question: When analyzing experimental data, under what condition should a bar chart be used instead of a line graph?
options: When the independent variable is categoric rather than continuous
When there are more than fifty data points to plot
When the dependent variable is measured in seconds or minutes
When the experiment has only one control variable

questions.question: How are wind-dispersed seeds typically adapted to their method of dispersal?
options: They are heavy and shaped like hooks to catch on passing animals.
They have fleshy, sweet-tasting coats to attract birds.
They are light and have a large surface area.
They are waterproof and float easily on streams.

questions.question: Why is it important to repeat measurements for each value in an investigation?
options: To ensure the independent variable changes automatically
To identify anomalous results and calculate a mean
To prove that no control variables are needed
To convert categoric data directly into continuous data
